## §13.1.1: Metric-Affine Qualia Geometry &amp; Non-Abelian Stokes–Wilson Holonomy {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: METRIC-AFFINE CURVATURE DECOMPOSITION &amp; WILSON HOLONOMY (DEF. 13.1 – THM. 13.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.1 (Metric-Affine Manifold Structure):**
Let $M_U$ be a cognitive context manifold equipped with generalized non-Hermitian metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = g + \omega$ (Riemannian metric $g$ + skew-symmetric torsion/vorticity 2-form $\omega$). On principal bundle $P_U \to M_U$ with connection $\mathbf{A} = A_0 + \sum a_k + a_{\mathrm{int}}$, the total curvature decomposes as:
$$
F_A \;=\; \sum_k \mathcal{F}_k^{(A_0)} \;+\; \Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.2 (Non-Abelian Stokes–Wilson Holonomy for Bound Qualia):**
Let $P_U \to M_U$ be a principal $G$-bundle over an orientable cognitive context manifold $M_U$ with connection $\mathbf{A} = A_0 + a_1 + a_2 \in \Omega^1(M_U, \mathfrak{g})$ where $a_1 \wedge a_2 \ne 0$, and let $\mathcal{C} = \partial \Sigma$ bound a compact 2-surface $\Sigma \subset M_U$:

1. **Wilson Loop Holonomy:** $\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathcal{C}) \coloneqq \mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A}\right) \coloneqq \lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{k=1}^N \exp\!\left(-\mathbf{A}(\dot{\gamma}(t_k))\Delta t\right)$.
2. **Non-Abelian Stokes Theorem:** $\tr\!\left(\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\mathcal{C})\right) = \tr\!\left(\mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} F_A\right)\right) = \tr\!\left(\mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} (\mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2])\right)\right)$.
3. **Pure Quale Commutator Phase Shift ($\mathcal{F}_1 = 0, \mathcal{F}_2 = 0$):**
$$
\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\partial \Sigma) \;=\; \mathcal{P}\exp\!\left(-\iint_{\Sigma} [a_1, a_2]\right) \;\ne\; \id_G
$$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proof of Theorem 13.2 (Dyson Series &amp; Plaquette Commutator):**
Parallel transport $\Gamma(t) \in G$ along $\gamma \colon [0,1] \to M_U$ satisfies $\frac{d}{dt}\Gamma(t) + \mathbf{A}(\dot{\gamma}(t))\Gamma(t) = 0$ with $\Gamma(0) = \id$, solved by the Dyson path-ordered series $\Gamma(1) = \id + \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n \int_0^1 dt_1 \dots \int_0^{t_{n-1}} dt_n \, \mathbf{A}(t_1)\dots\mathbf{A}(t_n)$. Subdividing $\Sigma$ into plaquettes $\delta\sigma_{ij} = \Delta x^i \wedge \Delta x^j$, orthogonal transport commutators yield $\Gamma_{\Delta x^i}^{-1}\Gamma_{\Delta x^j}^{-1}\Gamma_{\Delta x^i}\Gamma_{\Delta x^j} = \id - F_{ij}\Delta x^i\Delta x^j + \mathcal{O}(|\Delta x|^3)$. Surface integration gives $\Hol_{\mathbf{A}}(\partial\Sigma) = \mathcal{P}\exp(-\iint_\Sigma (\mathcal{F}_1 + \mathcal{F}_2 + [a_1, a_2]))$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

## §13.1.2–13.1.3: Functorial *Zeitkorn* ($\delta t_n$) &amp; Saccadic Object Constancy {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATA B &amp; C: CHRONOMETRIC QUANTIZATION (THM. 13.3) &amp; PERCEPTUAL OBJECT CONSTANCY (THM. 13.4, FIG. 13.2)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.3 (Functorial Chronometric Quantization — *Zeitkorn* $\delta t_n$):**
Let $\mathbb{T} \coloneqq \mathbb{N}_0$ act on the sheaf category $\Sh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{syn}}, \mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})$ by pushout endofunctor iteration $\rho(n) \coloneqq (YF_{\mathrm{model}})^n$:
$$
\mathfrak{f}_n \in \Sh \;\xrightarrow{\;YF_{\mathrm{model}}\;}\; \mathfrak{f}_{n+1} = YF(\mathfrak{f}_n), \qquad \delta t_n \;\coloneqq\; \tau(n+1) - \tau(n) > 0
$$
Subjective conscious duration is not a passive background continuum, but the discrete difference metric between functorial pushout updates (e.g., visual alpha gating at $\sim 10\,\text{Hz}$ and gamma binding cycles at $\sim 40\,\text{Hz}$, $\delta t_n \approx 25\,\text{ms}$).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.4 (Perceptual Object Constancy Theorem, Fig. 13.2):**
Let $\mathcal{C} = (B_1 \xrightarrow{\alpha_1} B_2 \xrightarrow{\alpha_2} \dots \xrightarrow{\alpha_Z} B_1)$ be a closed exploratory sensorimotor loop (e.g., ocular saccades or manual palpation). A perceptual feature $\mathbf{a} \in P^{B_1}$ represents an objective invariant entity iff its transport holonomy in the total fibration $\pi \colon \int_{\Ctx} \mathbf{Syn} \to \Ctx$ is an isometric identity:
$$
\Hol_{\mathbf{Syn}}(\mathcal{C})(\mathbf{a}) = \mathbf{a} \;\iff\; \oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{0}
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

  <video autoplay data-autoplay loop muted playsinline src="media/Ch13_Act2_Zeitkorn_Object_Constancy.mp4" style="max-height:215px;"></video>

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-left style="margin-top:8px;"}
**Why the World Does Not Spin When Your Eyes Move (Theorem 13.4):**
During a rapid ocular saccade $B_1 \xrightarrow{\alpha_1} B_2 \xrightarrow{\alpha_2} B_3 \xrightarrow{\alpha_3} B_1$, retinal coordinates shift violently, but corollary discharge (efference copy) supplies the exact compensatory connection 1-form $\mathbf{A}$ along $\mathcal{C}$ so that $\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{0}$. External object motion violates $\oint_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{0}$, cleanly separating self-generated retinal slip from external physical movement.
:::

:::

## §13.1.4: Intersubjective Faithfulness, Affinity Interfaces &amp; Theory of Mind {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATA B &amp; C: TWO-SIDED NON-DEGENERATE AFFINITY INTERFACES &amp; INTERSUBJECTIVE FAITHFULNESS (THM. 13.5)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.5 (Intersubjective Faithfulness &amp; Theory of Mind):**
Let $\mathcal{E}_A, \mathcal{E}_B$ be independent autopsychological toposes representing distinct observers mediated by a stabilized affinity interface $\beta^\infty \in \prod \Bil_{\le 1}(F_\gamma^A, F_0^B; \mathbb{R})$. Mutual intersubjective understanding is faithful and non-solipsistic iff the induced linear operators:
$$
T_\beta \colon F_0^A \longrightarrow (F_0^B)^*, \qquad S_\beta \colon F_0^B \longrightarrow (F_0^A)^*
$$
are strictly **two-sided non-degenerate**:
$$
\ker(T_\beta) = \{0\} \quad \text{and} \quad \ker(S_\beta) = \{0\}
$$
guaranteeing an injective, lossless embedding of subjective context frames without requiring identical physical substrate states.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Structural Resolution of Philosophical Solipsism:**
* Suppose observer $A$'s internal quale carrier $F_0^A$ has a non-trivial radical $\ker(T_\beta) \ne \{0\}$. Any internal state difference $v_1 - v_2 \in \ker(T_\beta)$ induces zero bilinear coupling $\beta^\infty(v_1 - v_2, w) = 0$ for all $w \in F_0^B$, rendering that aspect of $A$'s experience permanently incommunicable to $B$.
* Conversely, when $\ker(T_\beta) = \{0\}$ and $\ker(S_\beta) = \{0\}$, the curried transpose embeds $F_0^A \hookrightarrow (F_0^B)^*$ isomorphically onto its image: relational structure is faithfully transmitted across distinct biological or synthetic brains!
:::

:::

## §13.1.5: BRST Cohomology &amp; Grothendieck Fibration $\int_{\Ctx}\mathbf{Syn}$ {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: BRST GAUGE INVARIANCE &amp; GROTHENDIECK FIBRATION (THM. 13.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.6 (BRST Redundancy Elimination &amp; Grothendieck Fibration):**

1. **BRST Ghost-Number-Zero Cohomology:** The BRST differential $s_{\mathrm{BRST}}$ on the graded context configuration algebra $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}}$ satisfies exact nilpotency $s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 \equiv 0$. The true, observer-invariant phenomenal state space is the ghost-number-zero cohomology:
$$
\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{phenom}} \;\coloneqq\; H^0_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}}) \;=\; \frac{\ker s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=0}}{\operatorname{im} s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=-1}}
$$
which quotients out all arbitrary coordinate framing redundancies.
2. **Grothendieck Fibration:** The canonical projection $\pi \colon \int_{\Ctx}\mathbf{Syn} \to \Ctx$ from the total category of parameterized Syntrix algebras over parameter manifolds $M_U$ is a **Grothendieck Fibration**, ensuring every context transition $h \colon V \to U$ admits a universal Cartesian pullback lift $h^*(\underline{\mathbf{S}})$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Why Phenomenology Requires Gauge Cohomology ($s_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 = 0$):**
* Local cortical micro-columns constantly rotate their internal coordinate gauges without altering subjective perception (drift in single-neuron tuning curves despite stable population coding).
* Passing to $H^0_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ext}})$ mathematically eliminates unphysical gauge-ghost degrees of freedom ($\operatorname{im} s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=-1}$) while retaining physical gauge-invariant observables ($\ker s_{\mathrm{BRST}}|_{\mathrm{gh}=0}$).
:::

:::

When an observer shifts attentional context via $h \colon V \to U$, the Grothendieck fibration property guarantees a unique universal pullback $h^*(\underline{\mathbf{S}}) \to \underline{\mathbf{S}}$ through which any compatible cognitive state factorizes uniquely.

## §13.1.6: The $3 \times 3$ Taxonomic Property Grid $\hat{A} = (A_{ik})$ &amp; Singularities {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A &amp; B: 3×3 TAXONOMIC PROPERTY GRID (DEF. 13.7) &amp; SINGULARITY CLASSIFICATION (THM. 13.8)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.7 ($3 \times 3$ Taxonomic Property Grid $\hat{A} = (A_{ik})$):**
The $3 \times 3$ matrix $\hat{A} = (A_{ik})_{i,k=1}^3$ classifies cognitive transformation endofunctors $F \in \operatorname{End}(\Sh(\mathbf{Man}_{\mathrm{param}}))$ by:

* **Action Property ($i \in \{1,2,3\}$):**
  - $i=1$: Colimit-preserving (inductive synthesis / pushout).
  - $i=2$: Limit-preserving (projective constraint / pullback).
  - $i=3$: Isogonal equivalence (angle/metric-preserving gauge).
* **Effect Target ($k \in \{1,2,3\}$):**
  - $k=1$: Conflexive pushout nodes.
  - $k=2$: Tensor rank / manifold dimension alterations.
  - $k=3$: Field-intrinsic affine connections.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.8 (Topological Singularity Classification of $\hat{A}$):**
* **Singular Classes ($A_{12}, A_{22}$):** Strict dimensional compression ($A_{12}$: $\dim F(\mathcal{M}) < \dim \mathcal{M}$) and strict dimensional expansion ($A_{22}$: $\dim F(\mathcal{M}) > \dim \mathcal{M}$) produce **Class $A_{12}/A_{22}$ Dimension-Defect Singularities** (topological tearing of state space).
* **Geodesically Complete Classes:** Isogonal equivalences ($A_{31}, A_{32}, A_{33}$) and connection modulations ($A_{13}, A_{23}$) preserve smooth geodesic completeness across all parameter manifolds.
:::

:::

## §13.2.1: Telecentric Morse Separatrices &amp; DeTurck Parabolic Smoothing {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A &amp; B: LYAPUNOV STABILITY &amp; DETURCK SOBOLEV CONTRACTION PROOF (THM. 13.9 – THM. 13.10)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.9 (Morse Separatrices &amp; Televariant Lyapunov Stability):**
On complete Riemannian manifold $(\MAR, \gAR)$, the *Extinktionsdiskriminante* $\Dext \coloneqq \partial\mathcal{B}(T_z) = \bigcup_{j=1}^M W^s(p_j)$ is an invariant codimension-1 stable manifold of index-1 hyperbolic saddles separating the televariant attractor basin $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$ from dysvariant collapse into $\nullsyntrix$. Within $\mathcal{B}(T_z)$, the Lyapunov potential $V(x) \coloneqq \Psi(x) - \Psi(T_z)$ satisfies exponential dissipation $V(\Phi_t(x_0)) \le V(x_0)e^{-2\gamma t}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.10 (DeTurck Parabolic Smoothing &amp; Sobolev Fixed-Point Contraction):**
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold ($\partial\mathcal{M}=\emptyset$). Define the non-linear Ricci-like operator:
$$
\mathcal{T}(g)_{ij} \;\coloneqq\; -2R_{ij}(g) + \nabla_i V_j + \nabla_j V_i, \qquad V^k \coloneqq g^{pq}\!\left(\Gamma_{pq}^k(g) - \widetilde{\Gamma}_{pq}^k\right)
$$
For Sobolev index $s > \frac{n}{2} + 2$, the heat-smoothed cascade operator $\mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}} \coloneqq e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{g_0} + c_0 I)} \circ \mathcal{T}$ is a **strict contraction** on $\mathbf{B}_{H^s}(g_0, \delta) \subset H^s(\mathcal{M}, \Sym^2(T^*\mathcal{M}))$:
$$
\|\mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g_1) - \mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g_2)\|_{H^s} \;\le\; k_M \|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s} \quad (k_M < 1)
$$
converging uniquely to a smooth stationary apex metric ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$.
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Four-Step Proof of Theorem 13.10:**

1. **Strong Ellipticity:** The DeTurck term kills diffeomorphism gauge degeneracy; principal symbol $\sigma_\xi(\mathcal{T}(g))h_{ij} = g^{ab}\xi_a\xi_b h_{ij} = \|\xi\|_g^2 h_{ij}$ maps $H^s(\mathcal{M}) \to H^{s-2}(\mathcal{M})$.
2. **Banach Algebra Lipschitz Bound:** Since $s > n/2 + 2$, $H^s(\mathcal{M}) \hookrightarrow C^2(\mathcal{M})$ is a Banach algebra, giving $\|\mathcal{T}(g_1) - \mathcal{T}(g_2)\|_{H^{s-2}} \le C_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)\|g_1 - g_2\|_{H^s}$.
3. **Parabolic Smoothing:** $\|e^{-\tau_M(\Delta_{g_0} + c_0 I)}\|_{\mathcal{B}(H^{s-2}, H^s)} \le C_{\mathrm{heat}} \frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} \implies k_M \coloneqq C_{\mathrm{heat}}C_{\mathrm{geom}}(\delta)\frac{e^{-c_0\tau_M}}{\tau_M} < 1$ for large $\tau_M$.
4. **Banach Fixed Point &amp; Bootstrapping:** $g^{(n+1)} = \mathbf{\Phi}_{\mathrm{apex}}(g^{(n)}) \to {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_\infty \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})$ by elliptic regularity. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

**Theorem 13.11 (Universal Coalgebraic Dynamics &amp; *Telezentralenrelativität*):**
The basepoint-preserving trajectory functor $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}(M) \coloneqq (M \times C^\infty([0, \epsilon], M))_{\operatorname{ev}_0 = \operatorname{pr}_1} \amalg \mathbf{1}$ possesses a final coalgebra $(\nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}, \zeta)$ equipped with the Lambek isomorphism:
$$
\zeta \colon \nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}} \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}(\nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}), \qquad \exists! \; !_\alpha \colon (S, \alpha) \longrightarrow (\nu\mathcal{T}_{\mathbb{R}}, \zeta)
$$
Because the *Transzendenzsynkolator* $\Gamma_m \dashv U_{m+1}$ between scale strata $C(m) \to C(m+1)$ is a **left adjoint**, it preserves colimits rather than terminal limits:
$$
\Gamma_m(\nu\mathcal{T}_m) \;\not\cong\; \nu\mathcal{T}_{m+1}
$$
proving the mathematical relativity of telecentric attractors across hierarchical scales.

In the ambient higher $(\infty, 1)$-topos $\Xsyn \coloneqq \Sh_\infty(\Ctx, \Jsyn)$, structural abstraction and sensory noise filtering are governed by the **Postnikov $m$-Truncation Functor** $\tau_{\le m} \colon \Xsyn \to \Xsyn^{\le m}$, left adjoint to the inclusion $\iota_m \colon \Xsyn^{\le m} \hookrightarrow \Xsyn$:

\tau_{\le m} \;\dashv\; \iota_m \implies \Map_{\Xsyn}(\tau_{\le m} X, \, Y) \;\simeq\; \Map_{\Xsyn}(X, \, Y) \quad \forall Y \in \Xsyn^{\le m}
$$

* **$\tau_{\le 0}$ (0-Truncation):** Extracts discrete conceptual objects ($\pi_0$).

* **Noise Erasure ($k > 1$):** Filters out microscopic thermal/synaptic fluctuations ($\pi_k = 0$ for $k > 1$).

**Theorem 13.13 (Phenomenal Dimensionality Condensation Theorem):**
Let a multi-tier metric cascade condense on an $N$-dimensional manifold. Equating the total metric condenser capacity $Z_\omega(N) \coloneqq \omega^4 = N^4/16$ with the coordinate deformation capacity $Z_k(N) \coloneqq N^2 + \frac{N}{2}\binom{N}{2} = (N^3 + 3N^2)/4$ yields the characteristic polynomial:
$$
Z_\omega(N) = Z_k(N) \;\iff\; N^4 - 4N^3 - 12N^2 \;=\; N^2(N - 6)(N + 2) \;=\; 0
$$
Its unique positive nonzero root **$N = 6$** proves that stable perceptual consciousness condenses onto the 6D manifold **$R_6 \coloneqq R_4 \times S_2$**:

* **Spatio-Temporal Sector ($R_4$):** $x_1, x_2, x_3$ (3D sensory receptive geometry) + $x_4$ (1D functorial *Zeitkorn* flow $\delta t_n$).

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.14 (Affective Hermetry Decomposition &amp; Divergence Conservation):**
On $R_6 = R_4 \times S_2$, the non-Hermitian metric tensor ${}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}} = {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+ + {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-$ has 36 real components partitioned into:
$$
36 \;=\; \underbrace{21}_{\text{Symmetric } {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_+} \;+\; \underbrace{15}_{\text{Skew-Symmetric } {}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}_-}
$$
Symmetric components encode spatial extension and mesobaric homeostatic baselines; skew components encode attentional vorticity ($F_{\mu\nu}$ on $R_4$), approach-avoidance bias ($R_4 \times S_2$), and intentional agency ($[\partial_5, \partial_6]$ on $S_2$). The modified Einstein–Heim tensor satisfies:
$$
\operatorname{div}_{\bar{g}}\!\left[\Gamma_{(-)}^{(6,6)}\!\left({}^2\bar{\mathbf{R}} - \frac{1}{2}{}^2\bar{\mathbf{g}}\mathrm{R}\right)\right] \;=\; \mathbf{0}
$$

## §13.3.3–13.3.4: Isocline Foliations $\mathfrak{f}_A$, Morse–Bott Centers &amp; Seeley Nuclearity {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: MORSE–BOTT CRITICAL SUBMANIFOLDS (DEF. 13.15) &amp; SEELEY NUCLEAR FRÉCHET TENSORS (THM. 13.16)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.15 (Isocline Submersion Foliation $\mathfrak{f}_A$ &amp; Morse–Bott Centers):**
Let ${}^m\bar{A} \colon R_m \to \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \le m$) be a smooth cognitive field. On the regular locus $R_m^{\mathrm{reg}} \coloneqq \{y \in R_m \mid \rk(d({}^m\bar{A})_y) = d\}$, the level sets $\Sigma_c \coloneqq ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c) \cap R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}$ form a smooth **regular foliation $\mathfrak{f}_A$ of codimension $d$** (perceptual contour maps). Under Morse–Bott regularity, the critical locus of the intensity potential $\Phi(A) = \|A\|_{g_m}^2$ decomposes into disjoint smooth critical submanifolds:
$$
\Crit(\Phi \circ A) \;=\; \bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha, \qquad \dim Z_\alpha = d_\alpha \le m
$$
where the Hessian $\nabla^2(\Phi \circ A)|_{N Z_\alpha}$ is non-degenerate on the normal bundle $N Z_\alpha$, forming stable focal attention centers.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.16 (Seeley Super-Exponential Extension &amp; Nuclear Tensor Isomorphism):**
The Seeley extension operator $\mathcal{E}^{(n)} \colon \mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n) \to \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with regularized $q$-Pochhammer coefficients ($q = 1/2$) converges uniformly on orthant corners, establishing that $\mathscr{S}((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m)$ is a **nuclear Fréchet space**:
$$
\mathscr{S}\!\left((\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m\right) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{i=1}^{m,\pi} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}) \;\cong\; \widehat{\bigotimes}_{i=1}^{m,\varepsilon} \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})
$$
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up style="margin-top:8px;"}
**Why Nuclearity ($\widehat{\bigotimes}_\pi \cong \widehat{\bigotimes}_\varepsilon$) Matters for Multi-Modal Binding:**
Because biological firing rates are strictly non-negative ($x_i \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$), sensory fields live on orthant manifolds with corners $(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^m$. Theorem 13.16 guarantees that the projective ($\pi$) and injective ($\varepsilon$) topological tensor products coincide canonically, eliminating ambiguity between joint multi-channel distributions and continuous operator kernels!
:::

:::

## §13.3.5: Spectral Geometry of Selector Operators on Compact Fiber $K_8$ {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: HILBERT STATE SPACE ON K_8 = S² × T⁶ (DEF. 13.17) &amp; DISCRETE SPECTRAL HARMONICS (THM. 13.18)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Definition 13.17 (Hilbert State Space $\mathcal{H}_E$ on Compact Fiber $K_8$):**
Let $P \to M$ be a fiber bundle with compact 8D smooth boundaryless fiber:
$$
K_8 \;\coloneqq\; S^2 \times \mathbb{T}^6, \qquad \partial K_8 = \emptyset
$$
and let $E \to K_8$ be a Hermitian vector bundle. The **Hilbert State Space** is $\mathcal{H}_E \coloneqq L^2(K_8, E)$ equipped with the positive-definite Riemannian volume measure $d\mu_{K_8}$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.18 (Discrete Spectral Harmonics Theorem on $K_8$):**
The strongly elliptic self-adjoint selector operator:
$$
\operatorname{Sel} \;\coloneqq\; \Delta_E + \mathrm{i}\rho\!\left(\iota_{K_8}^*\Omegaint\right) \;\colon\; H^2(K_8, E) \subset \mathcal{H}_E \longrightarrow \mathcal{H}_E
$$
has purely discrete real point spectrum $\Spec(\operatorname{Sel}) = \{\lambda_k\}_{k=1}^\infty \subset \mathbb{R}$ with no finite accumulation point ($\lim_{k\to\infty}|\lambda_k| = \infty$), finite-dimensional eigenspaces, and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis:
$$
\operatorname{Sel}(\Psi_k) = \lambda_k \Psi_k, \qquad \langle\Psi_j, \Psi_k\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_E} = \delta_{jk}
$$
**Quantized cognitive attractors emerge as spectral harmonics of self-adjoint geometric selectors.**
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.proof-box}
**Proof of Theorem 13.18 (Rellich Compactness &amp; Spectral Resolution):**
1. **Self-Adjointness:** Since $\partial K_8 = \emptyset$, the connection Laplacian $\Delta_E = \nabla^*\nabla$ is essentially self-adjoint on $H^2(K_8, E)$. Because $\Omegaint$ takes values in a skew-Hermitian Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g} \subset \mathfrak{u}(N)$, multiplication by $\mathrm{i}\rho(\iota_{K_8}^*\Omegaint)$ is a bounded pointwise self-adjoint 0th-order perturbation.
2. **Compact Resolvent:** By **Rellich's Kondrachov Compactness Theorem** on the closed manifold $K_8$, the Sobolev embedding $H^2(K_8, E) \hookrightarrow L^2(K_8, E)$ is a compact operator.
3. **Discrete Eigenbasis:** Elliptic regularity implies that the resolvent $(\operatorname{Sel} - \lambda I)^{-1} \colon L^2 \to H^2 \hookrightarrow L^2$ is compact for $\lambda \notin \mathbb{R}$. The spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators with compact resolvent yields a complete orthonormal basis of smooth eigenfunctions $\{\Psi_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$ with real eigenvalues $|\lambda_k| \to \infty$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.3.6: Stokes–Cartan FEEC Discretization &amp; Metronic Lattice UV Cutoff {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: EXACT DE RHAM COCHAIN COMMUTATIVITY &amp; BRILLOUIN DISPERSION (THMS. 13.19 – 13.20)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.19 (Commutativity of the Stokes–Cartan Discretization Functor):**
Let $K$ be a regular cubical cell complex discretizing smooth orientable manifold $\mathcal{M}_n$ at linear mesh spacing $\sqrt{\tau} > 0$. The de Rham integration projection $(\mathcal{R}_\tau^k \omega)(\sigma_k) \coloneqq \int_{\sigma_k} \omega$ commutes strictly with the discrete coboundary $d_\tau$ in $\mathbf{Ch}_{\ge 0}(\mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}})$:
$$
d_\tau \circ \mathcal{R}_\tau^k \;=\; \mathcal{R}_\tau^{k+1} \circ d, \qquad \|\Pi_\tau^k \alpha - \alpha\|_{L^2} \;\le\; C_{\mathrm{approx}}\, \tau^{s/2} \|\alpha\|_{H^s} \;\; (0 < s \le 1)
$$
**3-Step Proof:** For $(k+1)$-cell $\sigma_{k+1}$ with boundary $\partial\sigma_{k+1} = \sum_j (-1)^j \operatorname{Face}_j(\sigma_{k+1})$:
(1) $((\mathcal{R}_\tau^{k+1}\circ d)\omega)(\sigma_{k+1}) = \int_{\sigma_{k+1}} d\omega$;
(2) $((d_\tau \circ \mathcal{R}_\tau^k)\omega)(\sigma_{k+1}) = (\mathcal{R}_\tau^k\omega)(\partial\sigma_{k+1}) = \int_{\partial\sigma_{k+1}}\omega$;
(3) Classical Stokes' Theorem $\int_{\sigma_{k+1}} d\omega = \int_{\partial\sigma_{k+1}}\omega$ equates both paths. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Corollary 13.20 (Metronic Lattice Momentum Dispersion &amp; UV Cutoff):**
On the uniform discrete metronic lattice $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n = \bigoplus_{i=1}^n \tau_i\mathbb{Z}$ ($\tau_i^2 = \tau$):

1. **Fourier Diagonalization:** $\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i\phi)(\mathbf{k}) = (1 - e^{-\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i})\widehat{\phi}(\mathbf{k})$ and $\mathcal{F}(\nabla_i^*\phi) = (e^{\mathrm{i}k_i\tau_i}-1)\widehat{\phi}(\mathbf{k})$.
2. **DEC 0-Laplacian Dispersion ($\Delta_\tau = \sum_i \tau_i^{-2}\nabla_i^*\nabla_i$):**
$$
\lambda(\mathbf{k}) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{2}{\tau_i^2}\!\left(1 - \cos(k_i\tau_i)\right) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{4}{\tau_i^2}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{k_i\tau_i}{2}\right) \;\ge\; 0
$$
3. **UV Cutoff &amp; Torus IR Gap:** On $\mathbb{M}_\tau^n$, $\sigma(\Delta_\tau) = [0, 4n/\tau]$ gives ultraviolet cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{UV}} = 2\sqrt{n}/\sqrt{\tau}$ ($4/\sqrt{\tau}$ for $n=4$); on a finite periodic $N$-torus ($k_i = \frac{2\pi m_i}{N\tau_i}$), the lowest non-zero mode $\mathbf{m}=(1,0,\dots,0)$ has strictly positive gap $\Delta E_{\min} = \frac{4}{\tau}\sin^2(\pi/N) > 0$.
4. **Intrinsic Mass Gap:** Requires non-vanishing mass term in $V_{\mathrm{gauge}}$ or compact holonomy. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.5: Topos Integrated Information $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$ vs. Classical IIT 4.0 {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATA A, B &amp; C: HOMOLOGICAL INTEGRATION INVARIANT &amp; POLYNOMIAL COMPLEXITY (DEF. 13.21 – PROP. 13.23)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="51%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Bottlenecks of Classical IIT 4.0 (Tononi) vs. Definition 13.21 ($\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$):**
Standard IIT 4.0 suffers from **(1) Combinatorial Intractability** ($\mathcal{O}(2^N)$ Minimum Information Partition search over $\mathcal{P}(V\times V)$, uncomputable for $N > 12$) and **(2) Arbitrary Probability Metrics** (extrinsic EMD/KL divergence). In Syntrometrie, for active network $\mathcal{N} = (\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}, \mathbf{A})$ covered by $\mathcal{U} = \{V_i \to U\}_{i=1}^m$, the **Topos Integrated Information Index** is:
$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P}) \;\coloneqq\; \left\|\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}}\right\|_{L^2\Omega^2} \;\cdot\; \exp\!\left(-\frac{\|\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)\|_{\check{C}^1}^2}{2\sigma_{\mathrm{tol}}^2}\right)
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.22 (Equivalence &amp; Superiority of $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$):**
$\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}$ satisfies all five IIT 4.0 axioms (Existence, Intrinsicality, Information, Integration, Exclusion) while resolving combinatorial complexity:

1. **Causal Independence (Zero Integration):** Uncoupled modules $P_1 \oplus_1 P_2 \implies [a_i, a_j] \equiv 0 \implies \Omegaint \equiv \mathbf{0} \implies \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}} = 0$.
2. **Descent Consistency (Exclusion):** Contradictory overlaps $s_i|_{V_{ij}} \ne s_j|_{V_{ij}} \implies \|\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)\| \to \infty \implies \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}} \to 0$ exponentially.
3. **Polynomial Complexity:** Computing $\binom{N}{2}$ pairwise Lie brackets $[a_i, a_j]$ along active edges $E \subset V\times V$ scales as **$\mathcal{O}(|E|) \le \mathcal{O}(N^2)$** vs. $\mathcal{O}(2^N)$ MIP cuts. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Proposition 13.23 (Explicit Three-Node $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Evaluation Across Regimes):**
For 3 modules with strengths $\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3$ and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators $\|T_k\| = 1/2$, curvature $\Omegaint^{\mathcal{D}} = \omega_1\omega_2 T_3 dx^1\wedge dx^2 + \omega_2\omega_3 T_1 dx^2\wedge dx^3 + \omega_3\omega_1 T_2 dx^3\wedge dx^1$ yields:

* **1. Bound Triad ($\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)=0$):** $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{bound}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\omega_1^2\omega_2^2 + \omega_2^2\omega_3^2 + \omega_3^2\omega_1^2}$.
* **2. Abelian Split:** All channels in an Abelian subalgebra $\implies \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{split}} = 0$.
* **3. Contradictory Rivalry ($\|\Def\| = \Delta v$):** $\Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{rivalry}} = \Phi_{\mathrm{topos}}^{\mathrm{bound}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(\Delta v)^2}{2\sigma_{\mathrm{tol}}^2}\right) \to 0$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.6.1: The Geometry of Self-Consciousness &amp; Lawvere Fixed Points {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATA A &amp; B: CURRY–HOWARD PROOF OF THE LAWVERE EGO FIXED-POINT THEOREM (THM. 13.24)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="52%"}

<h3 style="color:#FFD700; margin-top:0;">Resolving the Homuncular Regress of *Ich-Bewusstsein*</h3>

* How does a cognitive system achieve **self-awareness** (*Ich-Bewusstsein*) without triggering an infinite homuncular regress (an observer observing an observer observing...)?
* Following F. William Lawvere's (1969) categorical diagonal theorem, self-consciousness is not a separate meta-module, but the **invariant diagonal fixed point $e^* \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$** of the internal evaluation morphism in a cartesian closed category (CCC).

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Theorem 13.24 (Curry–Howard Categorical Proof of the Lawvere Ego Fixed Point):**
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a cartesian closed category with terminal object $\mathbf{1}$, internal evaluation object $\Omega$, and observer internal state space $A \in \Obj(\mathcal{C})$. If an internal evaluation morphism $\Phi \colon A \times A \to \Omega$ is **point-surjective** (its curried transpose $\hat{\Phi} \colon A \to \Omega^A$ has a right section on global elements), then **every endomorphism $f \colon \Omega \to \Omega$ possesses a fixed point** $y^* \in \Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \Omega)$:
$$
f \circ y^* \;=\; y^*
$$
In particular, the self-reflective diagonal $\Delta_A \colon A \to A \times A$ induces an invariant self-representation (**Ego Token**) $e^* \in \Hom(\mathbf{1}, A)$ satisfying:
$$
\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle \;=\; f\!\left(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle\right)
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-left}
**Complete Three-Step Diagram-Chase Proof of Theorem 13.24:**

* **Step 1 (Construction of the Diagonal Functional):**
  Let $\Delta_A \coloneqq \langle \id_A, \id_A \rangle \colon A \to A \times A$ be the canonical diagonal morphism. Define the self-evaluating diagonal arrow $\delta \coloneqq \Phi \circ \Delta_A \colon A \to \Omega$. Post-composing with $f \colon \Omega \to \Omega$ yields the modified diagonal functional:
  $$
  g \;\coloneqq\; f \circ \delta \;=\; f \circ \Phi \circ \langle \id_A, \id_A \rangle \;\colon\; A \longrightarrow \Omega
  $$
* **Step 2 (Currying &amp; Surjectivity Inversion):**
  By cartesian closure, $\Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(A \times A, \Omega) \cong \Hom_{\mathcal{C}}(A, \Omega^A)$ via exponential transpose $\hat{\Phi} \colon A \to \Omega^A$. The arrow $g \colon A \to \Omega$ corresponds under adjunction to a global element $\ulcorner g \urcorner \colon \mathbf{1} \to \Omega^A$. By point-surjectivity of $\hat{\Phi}$ on global elements $\Hom(\mathbf{1}, A) \to \Hom(\mathbf{1}, \Omega^A)$, there exists a representing global element (the **Ego Token** $e^*$):
  $$
  e^* \;\colon\; \mathbf{1} \longrightarrow A \quad \text{such that} \quad \hat{\Phi} \circ e^* \;=\; \ulcorner g \urcorner
  $$
* **Step 3 (Evaluation Along the Diagonal):**
  Uncurrying $\hat{\Phi} \circ e^* = \ulcorner g \urcorner$ implies that for all generalized elements $x \colon X \to A$:
  $$
  \Phi \circ \langle e^* \circ !_X, \; x \rangle \;=\; g \circ x \;=\; f \circ \Phi \circ \langle x, x \rangle
  $$
  Instantiating $X \coloneqq \mathbf{1}$ and setting $x \coloneqq e^* \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ yields $\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle = f(\Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle)$. Setting $y^* \coloneqq \Phi \circ \langle e^*, e^* \rangle \colon \mathbf{1} \to \Omega$ gives $f \circ y^* = y^*$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §13.6.2: Active Inference as Sheaf Descent Optimization (Thm. 13.25) {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-c">STRATUM C: FRISTON'S ACTIVE INFERENCE AS ČECH DESCENT &amp; LYAPUNOV MINIMIZATION (THM. 13.25, FIG. 13.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Theorem 13.25 (Active Inference Sheaf Descent Theorem — Friston Formalized):**
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{V_i \to U\}$ be a sensory covering family in predictive processing:

1. **Prediction Errors are Čech Descent Defects:** The discrepancy between top-down generative priors ($s_{\mathrm{prior}} \in \mathbf{P}(U)$) and bottom-up sensory data ($s_{\mathrm{sens}} \in \check{C}^0(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{P})$) is the Čech 0-coboundary:
$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pred}} \;\coloneqq\; \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) \;=\; d^0(s) - d^1(s) \;\in\; \check{C}^1(\mathcal{U}, \mathbf{A})
$$
2. **Free-Energy Minimization is Lyapunov Descent:** Variational Free Energy $F$ is identical to the Lyapunov potential $V(x) \coloneqq \Psi(x) - \Psi(T_z)$ on $\MAR$:
$$
\dot{F} \le -\gamma F \;\iff\; \dot{V}(x) \le -\gamma V(x) \quad (\text{Televariant Convergence to Prior } T_z)
$$
3. **Active Motor Action as Context Morphism:** When internal synaptic weight updates cannot eliminate $\Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s) \ne 0$, the agent executes an active motor action (saccade, locomotion) $\alpha \colon U \to U'$ shifting physical sensors to force $\Def_{\mathcal{U}'}(s') \to 0$.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.def-box}
**Figure 13.6: The Reflexive Self-Consciousness &amp; Active Inference Loop**
* **Top-Down Generative Prior ($U \in \Ctx$):** Representable sheaf $\mathbf{y}(U)$ projects prior expectation $s_{\mathrm{prior}} \in \mathbf{P}(U)$ onto sensory overlaps $V_{ij} = V_i \times_U V_j$.
* **Two Dual Descent Pathways to Eliminate $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pred}} = \Def_{\mathcal{U}}(s)$:**
  1. **Perceptual Inference (Internal Synaptic Tuning):** Gradient descent $\dot{V} \le -\gamma V$ updates internal model parameters toward telecentre $T_z$.
  2. **Active Inference (Motor Context Morphism):** Base morphism $\alpha \colon U \to U'$ re-orients sensory organs until pullback sections agree ($\Def_{\mathcal{U}'}(s') = 0$).
* **Lawvere Closure:** Closed at the base by the invariant ego-token $e^* = \operatorname{Self}$ satisfying $\Phi_{\mathrm{ego}}(e^*, x) = f(\Phi_{\mathrm{ego}}(x, x))$.
:::

<pre class="lean-code-card">import Mathlib
open CategoryTheory
namespace Syntrometrie.CognitiveArchitecture
structure ContextObject where
  D : Type
  P : Type
  C : Type
  [instD : NormedAddCommGroup D] [instDSpace : NormedSpace ℝ D] [instDFin : FiniteDimensional ℝ D]
  [instP : NormedAddCommGroup P] [instPSpace : NormedSpace ℝ P] [instPFin : FiniteDimensional ℝ P]
  [instC : NormedAddCommGroup C] [instCSpace : NormedSpace ℝ C] [instCFin : FiniteDimensional ℝ C]
  K : D →L[ℝ] (P →L[ℝ] C)
  K_contr : ‖K‖ ≤ 1
  z : P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] P
  zeta : D ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] D
structure ContextHom (U V : ContextObject) where
  alpha_D : U.D →L[ℝ] V.D
  alpha_D_contractive : ‖alpha_D‖ ≤ 1
  alpha_P : U.P →L[ℝ] V.P
  alpha_P_contractive : ‖alpha_P‖ ≤ 1
  alpha_C : U.C →L[ℝ] V.C
  alpha_C_contractive : ‖alpha_C‖ ≤ 1
  comm : ∀ (d : U.D) (p : U.P), alpha_C (U.K d p) = V.K (alpha_D d) (alpha_P p)
  cipher_z : ∀ p, alpha_P (U.z p) = V.z (alpha_P p)
  cipher_zeta : ∀ d, alpha_D (U.zeta d) = V.zeta (alpha_D d)</pre>

<pre class="lean-code-card">lemma opNorm_comp_le_one {E F G : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G]
    (f : E →L[ℝ] F) (g : F →L[ℝ] G) (hf : ‖f‖ ≤ 1) (hg : ‖g‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖g.comp f‖ ≤ 1 := by
  calc ‖g.comp f‖ ≤ ‖g‖ * ‖f‖ := ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le g f
    _ ≤ 1 * 1 := mul_le_mul hg hf (norm_nonneg f) zero_le_one
    _ = 1 := mul_one 1
instance : Category ContextObject where
  Hom U V := ContextHom U V
  id U := {
    alpha_D := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.D, alpha_D_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    alpha_P := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.P, alpha_P_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    alpha_C := ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ U.C, alpha_C_contractive := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le
    comm := fun _ _ =&gt; rfl, cipher_z := fun _ =&gt; rfl, cipher_zeta := fun _ =&gt; rfl
  }
  comp f g := {
    alpha_D := g.alpha_D.comp f.alpha_D
    alpha_D_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_D g.alpha_D f.alpha_D_contractive g.alpha_D_contractive
    alpha_P := g.alpha_P.comp f.alpha_P
    alpha_P_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_P g.alpha_P f.alpha_P_contractive g.alpha_P_contractive
    alpha_C := g.alpha_C.comp f.alpha_C
    alpha_C_contractive := opNorm_comp_le_one f.alpha_C g.alpha_C f.alpha_C_contractive g.alpha_C_contractive
    comm := fun d p =&gt; by dsimp; rw [f.comm d p, g.comm (f.alpha_D d) (f.alpha_P p)]
    cipher_z := fun p =&gt; by dsimp; rw [f.cipher_z, g.cipher_z]
    cipher_zeta := fun d =&gt; by dsimp; rw [f.cipher_zeta, g.cipher_zeta]
  }</pre>

<pre class="lean-code-card">/-- Collect constants occurring in an expression via AST fold (App. C, Module 6) -/
def constantsInExpr (e : Expr) : NameSet :=
  e.foldConsts NameSet.empty (fun n acc => acc.insert n)

partial def getTransitiveConstants (env : Environment) (root : Name) : NameSet :=
  let rec visit (curr : Name) (visited : NameSet) : NameSet :=
    if visited.contains curr then visited else
      let visited' := visited.insert curr
      match env.find? curr with
      | some info =>
          let visited1 := (constantsInExpr info.type).fold (fun acc c => visit c acc) visited'
          match info.value? with
          | some val => (constantsInExpr val).fold (fun acc c => visit c acc) visited1
          | none => visited1
      | none => visited'
  visit root NameSet.empty

def checkTransitiveFirewall (declName : Name) (tag : ProvenanceTag) : CoreM Unit := do
  let env &lt;- getEnv
  let deps := getTransitiveConstants env declName
  if tag.stratum == Stratum.StratumA || tag.stratum == Stratum.StratumB then
    if tag.type == EpistemicType.PhysicalHypothesis then
      throwError "EPISTEMIC FIREWALL BREACH: Stratum A/B declaration tagged [P]."
    for depName in deps do
      if let some depTag := provenanceMap.getState env |&gt;.find? depName then
        if depTag.type == EpistemicType.PhysicalHypothesis || depTag.stratum == Stratum.StratumD then
          throwError "EPISTEMIC FIREWALL BREACH: forbidden transitive dependency."</pre>
